chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: Looking back on the swing era
summary: He says every band had a recognizable style and he hated to see it end.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: All right. Are there any comments your would like to make, or observations that you would like to share with us on the Swing era or the big band era in general? You know, in terms of popularity or anything.

Well, the only comment I can make on that there was the good feeling through those years when the different bands started playing their own style. You know, everybody, if you had a band and had a style,

everybody recognized that band. You didn't have to look at a band and tell who that was, and who was playing. That's, well, everybody that had a little name had a big style. And, it's the same as I did.

Well, from dancing and listening at those people, it made you feel good. I don't know how to just explain that. But, it was a good feeling through those years, and I really enjoyed it. You don't know how much I enjoyed those years, and I really hated to see, see, I was one of the last bands to break down besides Count Duke and Cullin and, you know, a couple of other bands. You know, of course I hated to get rid of the big band and I went as long as I could. But, the way things was going, you know.
